A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same survey-based research. Their main text, tables, figures, and complete questionnaire and language-list appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original quantitative and qualitative findings from 81 survey responses, including project affiliations, motivations, resource limitations, and credit-attribution experiences.

after.justification: v4 retains the original 81-response survey and its quantitative and qualitative findings in Section 4, Table 1, and Figures 3–6.

M1.justification: Neither version proposes an algorithm or model architecture. The survey-based research approach remains unchanged.

E1.justification: Both study the same respondents working across more than 70 named languages, alongside language variants and families. Appendix A.2 retains the identical language inventory; no new population, task, or domain is studied.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates baseline methods against a proposed method. Additional references and discussion of earlier studies do not introduce empirical comparators.

E3.justification: Recruitment remains June–October 2024 through the same channels, with 81 responses. Appendix A.1 preserves the questionnaire, including optional questions, multiple-choice responses, and free-text fields; no sampling or analysis-procedure change is reported.

E4.justification: The same qualitative themes and incentive-by-duration breakdown are retained. Figure 6 already displays the duration categories in v1; v4's expanded explanation does not establish a new supplementary analysis.

E5.justification: Both report descriptive survey counts and percentages without confidence intervals, significance tests, or repeated-run and seed reporting. No uncertainty-estimation practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: Section 4.3 changes respondents lacking credit at least once from >80% to >67%, consistent with Figure 5's unchanged counts: 54 of 80 responses are not 'always'. Matching incentive plots by their category labels, v1 Figure 4 shows LLM research near 59, whereas v4 Figure 3 shows it near 25 despite retaining 59% in the text. These are localized reporting changes and inconsistencies, not evidence of changed survey data.

T1.justification: Neither version presents mathematical definitions, formal assumptions, theorems, or proofs. The conceptual framing around language and social power remains.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal contributions remain the same: document researchers' and workers' experiences, identify resource-quality and annotation-ethics problems, and recommend fairer practices. The conclusion retains the first-to-document claim.

C2.justification: v4 qualifies translation concerns by genre and native-speaker verification, elaborates recruitment pressure through promised professional prestige, and recommends per-language checks and disclosure of unresolved resource limitations. Section 5.3 removes some cultural-grouping examples and its checklist. The study's selection-bias limitation is unchanged.

D1.justification: Both supply the same questionnaire, language list, recruitment information, and confidentiality policy. v4 adds no implementation details or code/data access instructions; annotation-duration information was already present in v1.

R1.justification: v4 adds Birhane et al. (2022), Leech et al. (2024), and Mihalcea et al. (2024), extending discussion of participatory AI, questionable ML practices, and inclusive AI. Section 2 acknowledges additional prior case studies, while the overall positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: v4 makes grammar and terminology corrections, replaces a redundant numerical list accompanying Table 1 with prose, and condenses several recommendation and conclusion passages. The section sequence and appendix content remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v1 places the incentive and limitation plots under opposite captions. v4 aligns their category labels with the captions, although the revised incentive bars remain inconsistent with the text. Figures 3–5 have typography or legend changes, Figure 6 gains a fuller caption, and the appendices reflow. No figure or table is added.

improvement.justification: v4 corrects the inflated credit-attribution statement and adds useful qualifications about translation and worker exploitation. However, while addressing v1's swapped chart topics, it replaces the incentives-labelled plot's text-consistent values with conflicting bars, such as LLM research near 25 versus 59% in Section 4.2. The correction and clearer discussion coexist with this new numerical contradiction in a central result display, preventing a confident judgment of net overall improvement.
